reviewed_checks.finding: Separate class and entry point; StaticNetwork and solve_static retain their default operator.
Rejects supplied airflow, circulation, operating constraints, struts, engines and quiescent-fluid context.

Rejects rigid-frame rates/accelerations and actual elastic_motion or circulation_rate requests. Base residual always supplies a zero NetworkMotion object for static calls; its mere presence is not dynamic motion.
Requires surface chart, zero stepped-axis offsets and only rigid Ground/Joint types; checks complete section/CG offset and shear tables, not only sampled values.
Body-to-local T is transpose of saved local-to-body frame. K has c/s/n rows and phi/theta/psi columns; singular charts and principal-angle branch crossings reject.
Arithmetic endpoint T and K are used without orthogonalizing; body N/M are transformed after averaging.
E uses EIcc,GJ,EInn on c/s/n diagonal and symmetric EIcs,EIcn,EIsn couplings. Endpoint and averaged sections validate; stiffness_inverse preserves exact rigid directions.
Compliance is inverse of endpoint-averaged E, not the average of endpoint inverses, matching the visually checked Eq54 reading.
Eq48 position defect remains absolute; no unloaded curved-jig trapezoid defect is silently subtracted.
Subtracts K0_average times unloaded angle increment directly from current K_average times increment.
EA averaged before inversion and ds=unloaded arc remain explicit interpretations; no proof of historical executable semantics is claimed.
Endpoint-averaged mg/Dmg times unloaded length gives distributed weight, split equally to endpoints with no artificial distributed couple; signed-static flag remains required.
Point position is r+Q(original point-original node), with exact arm cross force transferred to node.
Retained rigid joint transfer is equal/opposite forces and T+(rj-ri) cross F versus -T; conserves total moment about any origin.
Both public derivative routes gate midpoint-specific mechanics on per-network analytic_mechanics; direct geometry also disabled for the alternative operator.
